title: Bound the Engram work-binding CLI reads on the dispatch path against the documented latency invariant
outcome: Every session bind now performs a synchronous two-command Engram CLI read (work next --sections focus, then work focus <id>) via read_work_binding (src/engram_host_adapter.rs:3634); each command is bounded at ENGRAM_WORK_BINDING_COMMAND_TIMEOUT (6 s) with one 250 ms lock retry, so roughly 12.25 s worst case per command and about 24.5 s for the pair, and the stale-fence recovery paths in prepare_engram_dispatch and deliver_engram_turn re-run a full bind once more. A single user prompt can therefore spawn up to about 8 Engram processes and block the send path for tens of seconds, contradicting docs/features/engram-host-adapter.md:375-377 (250 ms per call; a hung dispatch is never acceptable). Cap the total work-binding read budget per dispatch, cache the binding per routing token, or move the read off the hot path (see also tm-qc2h for the sidecar prewarm), reconcile the brief, and add a test asserting the end-to-end dispatch wall clock stays inside a stated bound when the CLI read is slow. Found by the Claude delegated reviewer (Medium); the consultant review had accepted the bound as a fault-only cost, the documented invariant is the stricter contract.
